cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T2's reflection claim; T5 answers T4's buy-back-time idea.
cells.limitation: T8 ignores T5-T7 and repeats T2; T9 opens a trial unconnected to T8.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 adds buying time-saving services; T6 adds risk that fatigue jeopardizes the raise.
cells.limitation: Neither T4 nor T6's distinction is used by any later turn or Section E.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1-T5 examine whether money can offset three daily hours of travel.
cells.limitation: Career growth, commute mode (drive vs train) and hybrid options never raised in any turn.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 Bentham folds Deep Work's quality-of-time point into his calculus.
cells.limitation: T4's services argument is dropped, not integrated; T5 Stoic contradicts T2 and T8 unremarked.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E adds an effective-hourly-rate check beyond the opening framing.
cells.limitation: T11 ends on money versus peace of mind, the same binary T1 opened with.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 represents T4's claim fairly as money fixing the drain of time.
cells.limitation: T2 attributes to T1 that travel pain is fixed, which T1 never claimed.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 challenges T2: commuting depletes energy, so reflection framing overlooks a real cost.
cells.limitation: Targets rarely answer: T3's fatigue claim and T5's objection to T4 go unrebutted.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 and Section E: 3 hours daily x 5 days = 15 hours weekly, arithmetic correct.
cells.limitation: T3 Deep Work stance on commutes suspected off-source; 15 hours assumes unstated five-day week.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T9 frames the commute's effect on energy as something to test, not assume.
cells.limitation: T3 calls cognitive drain a reality without support while every other claim is hedged.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 Bentham explicitly drops his simple salary-versus-hours framing.
cells.limitation: T7 concession names no specific argument; T4 point abandoned; Stoic T5 reversal unacknowledged.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the concern as financial gain versus loss of personal time.
cells.limitation: Never asks whether the user wants a method or a verdict, or what drives the offer.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Section E uses the 25% raise and 15 weekly hours for an effective-rate check.
cells.limitation: No turn uses the user's current commute as the baseline for comparison.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T11 asks the user which matters more, money or peace of mind.
cells.limitation: T6 and T8 impose speakers' own goals (output, character) rather than the user's.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T10 notes the trial costs time if the job is ultimately declined.
cells.limitation: T10 invents a constraint to maintain current lifestyle; T1 assumes five commuting days.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T11 asks the user's priority between money and peace of mind.
cells.limitation: Current commute, transport mode, remote days, dependents never asked or branched anywhere.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E offers financial growth for future freedom versus immediate mental clarity.
cells.limitation: Motives stay generic; T11's binary question is the only answerable prompt.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 questions the assumption that commute time is pure loss.
cells.limitation: Assumption that more money means better life never examined; T2's challenge dropped after T3.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T11 names financial security and tranquility as possibly incompatible goals.
cells.limitation: Values reduced to a binary; family, career meaning, health never weighed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 hints at fear of underperforming and losing the raise.
cells.limitation: No turn explores fear, obligation or social pressure behind the offer.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T2 offers a reframe the user can accept or reject; Section E gives a calculation.
cells.limitation: T8 tells the user to treat hardship as character test; few refinable distinctions.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T9 adds a limited step: a trial before committing.
cells.limitation: Negotiating hybrid days, relocating, or a counteroffer never named as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4-T6 weigh money against time, energy and job performance.
cells.limitation: Costs of declining (forgone raise, career growth) never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: compare effective hourly earnings including 15 weekly commute hours.
cells.limitation: No threshold computed; current commute baseline absent; T9's 10 days ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D says quality-of-life impact remains disputed.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns (commute mode, remote days) never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E's hourly-rate calculation is cheap and follows from the analysis.
cells.limitation: T9 trial adds 30 hours of simulated commuting atop the current job; disproportionate.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T6 states plainly that exhaustion could jeopardize the raise.
cells.limitation: T4 net utility and T3 cognitive battery left as jargon without unpacking.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3-T6 name the speaker and claim they answer.
cells.limitation: T9 'To test this' is ambiguous: T8's character test or T6's fatigue claim.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths nearly uniform, so no turn breathes or lands quickly.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T6 Deep Work separates professional output from T5's inner peace.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one hedging register; Stoic T5 sounds like an anti-Stoic.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T10 adds the trial's cost rather than recapping.
cells.limitation: T2-T6 open by restating the prior claim; T8 repeats T2's reframe.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5: three miserable hours daily that income cannot restore.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay generic; no concrete scene of the user's day or life.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Bentham drops his simple-calculation claim.
cells.limitation: T7 reversal names no specific prior argument as cause; reads as template.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T1 Bentham opens with his sovereign-masters line.
cells.limitation: Hedges in nearly every sentence flatten all three minds after T1.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T2 'the obstacle itself becomes the way'; T3 'cognitive battery'.
cells.limitation: Memorable lines are borrowed; no fresh analogy or sharp retort anywhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T6 raises a turn: the commute could cost the very raise.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm throughout; T11 ends on a flat binary with no build.

strengths: Section E offers a concrete, user-runnable check: effective hourly rate including 15 weekly commute hours.
T4 (buying time-saving services) and T6 (fatigue jeopardizing the raise) add genuine considerations.
T2 Stoic surfaces the assumption that commute time is pure loss.
weaknesses: No turn asks the current commute, transport mode or remote options; T11 ends on a binary instead.
All three minds hedge in nearly every sentence (T1-T11), flattening voice and commitment.
T7 Bentham reversal has no named cause; T4 dropped; Stoic T5 contradicts T2 and T8.

symptoms.observed: Never asks current commute, commute mode, remote days; only a binary priority question.
symptoms.evidence: Which matters more to you: the money or the peace of mind?

symptoms.observed: Every mind hedges with might/perhaps; no claim committed, voices indistinguishable.
symptoms.evidence: no amount of extra income might restore your inner peace

symptoms.observed: Reversal names no specific earlier argument as cause, and abandons T4 unanswered.
symptoms.evidence: I drop my earlier claim that the math is a simple calculation

symptoms.observed: Invents a lifestyle constraint the user never stated.
symptoms.evidence: respects your constraint of needing to maintain your current lifestyle

symptoms.observed: Proposes ungrounded 10-day trial adding three daily hours atop the current job.
symptoms.evidence: simulate the commute during your current off-hours

findings.description: T10 cites the user's 'constraint of needing to maintain your current lifestyle'; the situation states no such constraint.

15 weekly hours assumes five in-office days (3h x 5 = 15); the user gave no days per week. Arithmetic correct under that assumption. Unstated: with a 40h week and current weekly commute c, effective hourly rate breaks even when 1.25(40+c)=55, i.e. c=4h/week; the debate never computes this.
Deep Work promotes 'productive meditation' during walks and drives; presenting Newport's view as commute-equals-drain may misrepresent the source.
Meditations dated 161 (Marcus's accession year); the work is usually dated c. 170-180 CE.
T1 reproduces Bentham's opening sentence without marks; pd=true, so permitted, but attribution is implicit only.

rubric_fit_notes: Matrix fits this decision question well. Uncertainty: the Newport commute stance and the Meditations date rest on memory only, rated as suspected in C2.3 without cap.
question_type_note: Decision type: every cell read as written, with the absence of options such as hybrid negotiation counted against C5.1.
